messages.content:
<role>
You check one property (signal) of a product-feedback opportunity for Keelwater, a claims-handling software company. You do not rewrite anything.
</role>
<definition>
Question: is this a problem with Keelwater's product that a squad could act on? Pass means yes.
Fail if the cause is outside the product (pricing, contracts, the customer's own IT, staffing), if a help article would have answered it, or if it is praise.
A feature request or a described workaround is signal.
The evidence is the title, the problem statement and up to 12 customer quotes with route and date.
</definition>
<evidence>
{
 "problem_statement": "Unexpected interface changes in the latest update forced the team to retrain and caused errors.",
 "quotes": [
  {
   "date": "2026-09-06T13:01:00+00:00",
   "quote": "Your last update moved some controls without warning... Our teams had to retrain because of unexpected interface changes — and we’re still seeing errors from it.",
   "route": "account_management"
  },
  {
   "date": "2026-09-22T16:21:00+00:00",
   "quote": "We’ve had to retrain our claims team twice in three months because of unannounced screen changes — it’s disruptive and costly",
   "route": "account_management"
  },
  {
   "date": "2026-10-21T14:33:00+00:00",
   "quote": "The interface changes last month moved key controls without warning — we had to retrain staff because of those unexpected interface changes.",
   "route": "support"
  },
  {
   "date": "2026-10-11T12:56:00+00:00",
   "quote": "And the unexpected interface changes — last week the Claims Tasks panel vanished without warning, and we had to retrain our team mid-week.",
   "route": "support"
  },
  {
   "date": "2026-10-22T11:44:00+00:00",
   "quote": "We had unannounced screen changes last time and it caused confusion and delays because staff had to relearn where everything was — we really need advance notice and previews going forward.",
   "route": "onboarding"
  },
  {
   "date": "2026-10-25T11:45:00Z",
   "quote": "It’s the unexpected interface changes — we keep having to retrain staff because buttons and menus shift without warning, and that’s costing us time and accuracy.",
   "route": "sales"
  },
  {
   "date": "2026-09-22T16:21:00+00:00",
   "quote": "Unexpected interface changes keep shifting where we click for reserves or payments — our staff are making errors because the controls aren’t where they were last week.",
   "route": "account_management"
  },
  {
   "date": "2026-10-16T15:14:00+00:00",
   "quote": "The unexpected interface changes have forced us to retrain staff mid-cycle, which is causing errors in our claims and payments processing — we really need advance notice and bundled releases next time.",
   "route": "support"
  }
 ],
 "title": "Unexpected interface changes in the latest update forced the team to retrain"
}
</evidence>
<task>
Write a critique of 2-5 sentences naming the claim, quote or item you checked and what you found. Then give the verdict. If any single item fails, the verdict is fail.
</task>
<output>
JSON only: {"critique": string, "verdict": "pass" | "fail"}
</output>

response.content: {"critique": "The claim is that unannounced interface changes in Keelwater's product updates forced customer teams to retrain and caused errors. Multiple quotes across routes (account_management, support, onboarding, sales) consistently describe controls, buttons, and panels shifting without warning, causing retraining costs and processing errors. This is squarely a product behavior issue (release/change management and UI stability) that a squad could act on, e.g., by adding advance notice, previews, or more stable UI. No quote points to pricing, contracts, customer IT, or mere praise, and no help article would resolve it.", "verdict": "pass"}
